findings.evidence: Integral.lean:96 `theorem isBernsteinFunction_bernsteinPrimitive … IsBernsteinFunction (bernsteinPrimitive c f)` vs Integral.lean:124-125 `theorem isBernsteinFunction_integral … IsBernsteinFunction (bernsteinPrimitive 0 f)`; grep shows `integral_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_Ici_eq_sub`, `integral_Ioi_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one` in CompletelyMonotone/Integral.lean use `integral` for genuine integrals.
findings.issue: `isBernsteinFunction_integral` states `IsBernsteinFunction (bernsteinPrimitive 0 f)`, but its name says `integral`, not the term actually in the conclusion; its general form one declaration above is `isBernsteinFunction_bernsteinPrimitive`, so the two names for the same object diverge. `integral_*` names are already used in `TauCeti/Analysis/CompletelyMonotone/Integral.lean` for actual interval integrals.

findings.evidence: Integral.lean:46-47 `noncomputable def bernsteinPrimitive (c : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := c + ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..t, f (max x 0)` — no hypothesis on `f` or `c`; Integral.lean:68-70 `hasDerivAt_bernsteinPrimitive` requires only `ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)`.
findings.fix: Name the construction for what it is, e.g. `primitiveIci c f` or `halfLinePrimitive`, and rename the derived lemmas to match; keep `IsBernsteinFunction` only in the conclusions that actually establish it.
findings.issue: `bernsteinPrimitive (c f t)` is defined for arbitrary `f : ℝ → ℝ` and arbitrary `c`, so the name advertises a property the object does not have — nothing about `c + ∫₀ᵗ f (max x 0)` is Bernstein until `hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f` and `0 ≤ c` are supplied. All the value/derivative lemmas (`bernsteinPrimitive_zero`, `hasDerivAt_bernsteinPrimitive`, `deriv_bernsteinPrimitive`) hold for any continuous `f` and inherit the misleading name.

findings.evidence: Integral.lean:51-52 `theorem bernsteinPrimitive_eq {…} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : bernsteinPrimitive c f t = c + ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..t, f x` vs the definition at Integral.lean:47; the addendum reserves `_def` for `foo = <its definition>`, which this is not.
findings.fix: Rename to describe the right-hand side and the hypothesis, e.g. `bernsteinPrimitive_eq_add_integral_of_nonneg` (or `…_of_nonneg`).
findings.issue: `bernsteinPrimitive_eq` reads as the definitional-unfolding lemma, but the definitional right-hand side is `c + ∫₀ᵗ f (max x 0)`; this lemma states the different, hypothesis-gated equality `c + ∫₀ᵗ f` for `0 ≤ t`.

summary: The construction and its lemmas are named after a property ("Bernstein") that the definition does not carry, and the c = 0 corollary breaks the naming symmetry with its own general form by calling itself `_integral`.
